title: Pro-Israel Pressure Group Honest Reporting Received Grant from Knight Foundation
author: Liam Syed
content:
As a reader-funded independent news outlet, we operate free from the influence
of governments, advertisers, and corporate backers. This is essential to our
mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that
spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for
everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary
support of our community of readers. Please consider making a[ tax-deductible
donation to support our work today](https://givebutter.com/dsn-substack).

post-
media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0069de1b-92b6-46a3-96ca-c528a7c5bf7a_4032x3024.jpeg)Palestinian
journalists protest against the assassination of their colleague Hassan
Eslaiah, outside Nasser Hospital, in Khan Yunis, Gaza on May 13, 2025. Eslaih
was killed in an Israeli attack on Nasser Hospital. Photo by Alaa Y. M.
Abumohsen/Anadolu via Getty Images.

Honest Reporting, a self-described media watchdog and nonprofit with offices
in New York, Jerusalem, and Toronto, [claims](https://honestreporting.com/our-
work/) that its mission is exposing "media bias, challenging false narratives,
and ensuring that reporting on Israel is rooted in facts, context, and
accountability." In practice, it operates as a pressure group, monitoring
international media coverage of Israel, producing reports attacking coverage
it deems unfavorable, running access operations that embed international
journalists within curated pro-Israel perspectives, and organizing mass
campaigns directing its subscribers to contact newsrooms directly until
corrections, retractions, and rewordings are secured.

That work has led to the dismissal of journalists at publications around the
world. But since October 7, 2023, Honest Reporting's operations have moved
into considerably darker territory, and its activities have contributed to the
assassination of at least one journalist, Hassan Eslaiah--a freelance
photographer and director of the Gaza-based Alam24 news agency whose images
had appeared in the Associated Press and CNN.

The campaign against Eslaiah was not isolated. Honest Reporting has
systematically targeted journalists and news organizations--including Drop
Site News--across multiple platforms and countries, employing consistent
tactics: publishing posts raising questions about individual journalists'
alleged connections to Hamas or other armed groups, characterizing their
coverage as propaganda or as "antisemitic," and mobilizing its subscriber
network to contact news organizations directly. The cumulative effect of this
approach has been to characterize numerous Palestinian journalists as
combatants.

Despite its record as a pressure group that targets and endangers reporters,
in 2023 Honest Reporting's Israeli organization--registered under the name
Divuach Ne'eman R''A--received an "emergency" grant of $100,000 from the
Knight Foundation, a widely respected U.S.-based foundation that prominently
touts a commitment to freedom of press and the safety of journalists. The
grant, listed in Honest Reporting's Israeli nonprofit filings for 2024, is not
reported in the Knight Foundation's 990 for 2024 or on its website.

The Knight Foundation [says](https://knightfoundation.org/how-we-fund/) that
it primarily funds U.S.-based organizations and that international programs
and organizations are among the categories it generally prefers not to fund,
making grants outside the United States limited and exceptional by the
foundation's own description. Knight's website
[states](https://knightfoundation.org/how-we-fund/) that "most of our
grantmaking is tied to strategies with defined goals and outcomes" and that
funding "typically emerges through relationships, research and ongoing work,"
with most grants initiated by Knight itself rather than through open
applications.

When approached for comment, Atena Sherry, Knight Foundation's director of
communications, initially denied that Knight had provided funding to Honest
Reporting: "Knight Foundation did not provide any grant to Honest Reporting,
and the foundation has not directed any Knight funds to Honest Reporting"
through any third party, Sherry told Drop Site. In a follow-up statement,
Sherry said, "We reviewed all documentation. Knight Foundation has never
provided any funding to Honest Reporting."

According to Honest Reporting, however, "the grantor, Jewish Federations of
North America and United Israel Appeal, notified Divuach Ne'eman R"A and
HonestReporting.com, Inc. that a donation of $100,000 was made 'on the
recommendation of the donor, The Knight Foundation.' Honest Reporting added
that "Staff for Divuach Ne'eman R"A and Honest Reporting.com, Inc. were in
direct touch with staff at the Knight Foundation throughout the process on the
grant and the programs that would benefit from the grant."

When Drop Site then asked the Knight Foundation about Honest Reporting's
statement, which directly contradicted its own, the Knight Foundation
acknowledged that it had provided funds for Media Central, an Honest Reporting
program that arranges tours for international journalists. "Knight Foundation
did make a one-time, emergency grant of $100,000 in November 2023 to Media
Central to support a very specific project: helping international journalists
to gain access they wouldn't otherwise have had to report on the facts from
the ground in the West Bank," said Alejandro de Onis, vice president for
communications, in a statement. "Neither the grant agreement nor the grant
file contains any reference to Honest Reporting."

Unlike Gaza, the West Bank has remained accessible to international
journalists, raising the question of what access Media Central was providing
that journalists could not obtain independently, and whether the access in
question was in fact embedded reporting alongside the Israeli military.

Knight declined to answer additional questions about the specific reporting
funded by its grant or how it could have been unaware that Media Central was a
program operated by Honest Reporting.

Through its Media Central project, Honest Reporting arranges press tours,
briefings, and curated access to Israel for international correspondents,
[presenting itself](https://www.m-central.org/about-us/) as a neutral resource
while functioning as an operation designed to shape how journalists understand
and cover the country. Honest Reporting's director of press relations, Laura
Cornfield, runs the program.

In Honest Reporting's 2023 first quarter [impact
repor](https://web.archive.org/web/20240403110438/https://honestreporting.com/landing_pages/mc-2023-first-
quarter-report/)t, Cornfield wrote that: "Journalists met with locals to hear
how the Lions' Den terrorist group was using Nablus as its command center.
They were then briefed by the IDF to understand the security risks to Israeli
civilians," boasting that "MediaCentral staff enabled exclusive access to
these unheard, nearly impossible-to-reach voices. The tour was so sought after
it was repeated with three groups, and an additional three one-on-one tours
were arranged."

In that year's second quarter [impact
report](https://web.archive.org/web/20240326080925/https://honestreporting.com/landing_pages/mc-2023-second-
quarter-report/), Cornfield wrote that the group's Media Central program "took
foreign media outlets on exclusive tours to hotbeds of terror activity,
including Nablus and Jenin, to get an up-close look at what Israeli security
forces are facing and how they are addressing the threats." The reports say
that journalists from prominent international outlets including the New York
Times, the Wall Street Journal, the Economist, the Financial Times, and CNN
have participated in its events.

The impact report described a media tour of the Israel-Lebanon border, quoting
the Israeli military's Lt. Gen. Herzi Halevi and Military Intelligence
Directorate chief Aharon Haliva on Hezbollah. It also included a section on
"crime in the Arab sector" and said that journalists had gone on "a field tour
to Umm Al Fahm and Jaffa of Nazareth to address the surging crime rate,"
referring to largely Palestinian towns and cities within Israel.

More recently, Media Central press tours have taken international journalists
to the[ ](https://x.com/MediaCentralJer/status/2026989732152951029/photo/1)Al
Aqsa compound and [Western Wall
Tunnels](https://x.com/MediaCentralJer/status/2026989732152951029/photo/2) in
occupied East Jerusalem and to [northern
Israel](https://x.com/MediaCentralJer/status/2041419748135616929/photo/1).
Media Central has also hosted exclusive briefings for international
journalists with senior Israeli political figures, including a [recent
lunch](https://x.com/MediaCentralJer/status/2071871170748543344/photo/1) in
Tel Aviv with former Israeli Ambassador to the United States Michael Oren and
an[ "exclusive
dinner](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7489755764383920128/)"
with Brigadier General (Res.) Pinchas (Pini) Yungman. Yungman has held senior
command roles in the Israeli Air Force and executive positions at the Israeli
defense company Rafael.

None of the briefings or meetings organized by Media Central appear to have
been led by Palestinians.

## "We don't claim to be a news organization."

On November 8, 2023, one month into the genocide in Gaza and the same month as
the Knight Foundation grant, Honest Reporting published what it classified as
an [expose](https://honestreporting.com/photographers-without-borders-ap-
reuters-pictures-of-hamas-atrocities-raise-ethical-questions/) on its website.
The article featured photographs of several Palestinian freelance journalists
who had been covering the events near the Gaza border on the morning of
October 7, among them Hassan Eslaiah. It asked, in language the organization
has since described as just "raising questions," whether these journalists
could have had advance knowledge of the Hamas attack. The article was then
updated to feature a photograph from 2020 of Eslaiah next to Hamas leader
Yayha Sinwar--clearly suggesting guilt by association through proximity in a
photograph.

Within hours, Israel's official X account had
[amplified](https://x.com/Israel/status/1722557456662802839) the post to its
own audience of 1.8 million. The Associated Press reviewed its relationship
with Eslaiah and later [severed](https://www.ap.org/the-definitive-
source/announcements/ap-statement-on-gaza-freelancers/) it, while stating
publicly it had found no evidence he had foreknowledge of the attack beyond
what was known to journalists routinely working in the border area. When the
AP asked Gil Hoffman, then Honest Reporting's executive director, to
substantiate the allegations, his
[response](https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-photographers-
attack-200be1ba47361f1c1fc113cdaeb65d04) was notable. "They acted as if we
were stating facts instead of asking questions," Hoffman said. "We don't claim
to be a news organization."

Jonthan Dagher, head of the Middle East desk of Reporters Without Borders
(RSF), described the November 2023 Honest Reporting article as being "full of
conjecture" and "based on circumstantial evidence," noting that it "provoked a
chain of reactions from Israeli authorities and politicians who started
accusing Gazan journalists of belonging to Hamas."

RSF named Honest Reporting in its 2025 list of Press Freedom Predators that it
says "smear media and promote mistrust of journalists."

Eighteen months later, in April 2025, an Israeli airstrike struck a media tent
outside Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis,
[killing](https://cpj.org/2025/04/israel-strikes-journalists-tent-in-
gaza-1-killed-8-injured/) two journalists and wounding eight others, Eslaiah
was among them. The Israeli military publicly
[announced](https://x.com/IDF/status/1909215556508512680) it had deliberately
targeted Eslaiah, claiming he was a member of the Khan Younis Brigade and had
participated in the attacks of October 7th. Eslaiah survived the strike but
his skull was fractured, his body was burned, and he lost two of his fingers.
He was admitted to Nasser Hospital's burns unit to recover. On May 13, 2025,
while he lay in the burn unit, an Israeli drone bombed the hospital and
murdered him. Hours later, the Israeli military admitted to assassinating
Eslaiah, calling him "Aslih" and
[posting](https://x.com/IDF/status/1922381573514551333) a screenshot of
Eslaiah on Oct. 7, 2023 from a video also posted by Honest Reporting in its
"expose" and saying: "Don't let Aslih's press vest fool you…Journalist? More
like terrorist."

## Targeting Palestinian Journalists

Since the start of the genocide in Gaza, one of Honest Reporting's central
goals has been to challenge the records kept by press freedom organizations
documenting Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza. The organization has led a
sustained pressure campaign against the Committee to Protect Journalists
(CPJ), which maintains the most widely cited casualty list of media workers
killed in Gaza. It has also sought to attack and pressure other press freedom
bodies such as [Reporters Without Borders](https://honestreporting.com/rsfs-
journalist-deaths-report-raises-alarming-questions-about-transparency/) and
the [International Federation of Journalists](https://honestreporting.com/ifj-
silently-removes-8-terrorism-linked-individuals-from-slain-gazan-journalist-
list/).

On June 25, CPJ [announced](https://cpj.org/2026/06/cpj-undertakes-review-of-
its-documentation-of-journalists-killed-in-israel-gaza-war-since-2023/) that
it would be "conducting a full review of its database of journalists killed
during the Israel-Gaza War." Honest Reporting was quick to
[claim](https://x.com/HonestReporting/status/2071908854904869344?s=20)
victory, [stating](https://x.com/HonestReporting/status/2071908838555484651)
that the review had happened because Honest Reporting had "helped put them in
an untenable position."

In a statement, CPJ denied that Honest Reporting's pressure campaign was
responsible for its database review.

"The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) is an independent organization. We
independently research, source and report information related to attacks on
journalists and media workers. When new information becomes available, we
update our reporting. Our review of the Israel-Gaza war casualties list was
spurred by new information published by Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad
that identified as combatants individuals previously listed by CPJ as
journalists. Honest Reporting's campaign had absolutely no bearing on the
review process or on the decision to remove names from the list."

CPJ, which receives major funding from the Knight Foundation, did not respond
to questions about the foundation's grant to Honest Reporting.

"We condemn any misrepresentation of that process to serve political agendas
or to try to obscure the fact Israel has killed more journalists than any
other country in the world and been the leading killer of journalists for the
past three years," CPJ said in its statement.

In response to questions about the direct conflict of interest entailed by
funding both a press freedom organization that maintains a database of
journalists killed by Israel and a pressure group that targets Palestinian
journalists, the Knight Foundation said, "The funding directed to Media
Central was specifically and only earmarked to facilitate journalists' access
to report on the war in hard to reach areas and there is no ongoing
relationship. Nothing in Knight Foundation's grant records reflects any
reference to a campaign concerning CPJ, and Knight Foundation has never funded
advocacy directed at CPJ."

On the same day that CPJ announced its Gaza database review, Jacob Weisberg,
chair of CPJ's board of directors, [emailed fellow board
members](https://www.cjr.org/the_media_today/who-counts-committee-protect-
journalists-cpj-definition-gaza-israel-war-conflict-hamas-idf-combatants.php)
to say that he was establishing a "special task force to reexamine the
question of 'Who is a journalist?'"

According to [reporting](https://www.cjr.org/the_media_today/who-counts-
committee-protect-journalists-cpj-definition-gaza-israel-war-conflict-hamas-
idf-combatants.php) in the Columbia Journal Review, Weisberg's initiative was
separate from the database review and grew out of a board discussion of an
article in the right-wing Washington Free Beacon that largely repackaged
Honest Reporting's attacks on CPJ and news organizations that report
critically on Israel, including Drop Site.

Nika Soon-Shiong, publisher of Drop Site News and a member of the CPJ board,
was alarmed by Weisberg's email and requested a vote on the proposal by the
full board, according to a letter she posted publicly. She was then informed
by Weisberg that her term on the board had expired. On July 1, the board held
an emergency meeting and voted to [affirm](https://cpj.org/2026/07/board-
votes-to-affirm-cpjs-existing-definition-of-who-is-a-journalist/) its
"existing definition of who is a journalist."

## Broader Influence Network

Honest Reporting's sustained attempts to establish connections between
journalists and armed groups, such as Hamas, is particularly striking given
the organization's direct ties to AIPAC, the Israeli government, and the
Israeli military, which continues to carry out a genocide in the Gaza Strip.

Prior to co-founding Honest Reporting, [Lenny Ben-
David](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lenny-bendavid-79826148/) spent 25 years at
AIPAC, including 15 years directing its Jerusalem office, before serving three
years as deputy chief of mission at the Israeli embassy in Washington. He has
[recounted](https://x.com/lennybendavid/status/1705904601143144854) with
evident pride how an early Honest Reporting campaign crashed CNN's internet
servers. The organization he helped build is now
[led](https://honestreporting.com/honestreporting-announces-appointment-of-
jacki-alexander-as-new-global-ceo/) by [Jacki
Alexander](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jackialexander/), who spent
approximately 15 years at AIPAC before being hired with a mandate to expand
Honest Reporting's reach in the United States.

National Development Director [Rebecca
Shimonovitc](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rebecca-shimonovitc-b936ba19/) spent
more than eight years as an AIPAC regional director before moving into Honest
Reporting's fundraising operation. [Justin
Pozmanter](https://www.linkedin.com/in/justin-pozmanter-4524001/) worked in
AIPAC's political department for over ten years before [relocating to
Israel](https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/author/justin-pozmanter), where he
served as a senior foreign policy advisor to Israeli government minister
Tzachi Hanegbi, and then joined Honest Reporting. [David
Barish](https://honestreporting.com/governance-and-finance/), treasurer of
Honest Reporting's U.S. organization, has
[held](https://kiwanishouston.org/event-5476037) positions on the boards of
AIPAC's Houston Council, Friends of the IDF, the Jewish Federation, Anti-
Defamation League, and the United Israel Appeal. He is also
[listed](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/134174402/202503079349301755/full)
as a director of the Foundation for the Defense of Democracies, a pro-Israel
think tank. [Laura Cornfield](https://www.linkedin.com/in/laura-
cornfield-988544142/), the group's director of press relations, also runs the
[Media Central](https://www.m-central.org/) program. She attends high-level
events within Israeli political circles posing and smiling with U.S ambassador
to Israel [Mike
Huckabee](https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=32839307042350535&set=pb.100000939883128.-2207520000&type=3)
and [Sara
Netanyahu](https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=31305487549065833&set=pb.100000939883128.-2207520000&type=3).

The connections to the Israeli military are equally direct. Multiple staff
members served in the Israeli military, a fact Honest Reporting says "should
not be a surprise" given Israel's mandatory service requirement. [Gil
Hoffman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gil-hoffman-9b3660248/), former executive
director and current board member, for example,
[served](https://www.icja.org/smooth-sailing-in-israel/) in an Israeli army
artillery unit and later as an Israeli military reserve spokesperson following
his emigration to Israel, before his journalism career at the Jerusalem Post.
Editorial Director [Simon Plosker](https://www.linkedin.com/in/simonplosker/)
has also served in the Israeli military's press office. [Rachel
Safdie](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rachel-safdie-048b30225/), who now appears
as a [reporter](https://www.instagram.com/p/DZaubcAiNz1/?hl=en) in Honest
Reporting's social media output, spent more than two years in the Israeli
military press office, where she served as head of its Iranian-language social
media desk.

In a statement, Honest Reporting denied that it has a formal relationship with
the Israeli military. "There is no formal affiliation or partnership between
the IDF and Divuach Ne'eman R"A or HonestReporting.com, Inc."

Honest Reporting was launched in 2000 in association with the Jerusalem Fund
of Aish HaTorah, an Orthodox Jewish outreach movement whose stated mission is
encouraging secular Jews to embrace religious observance, but which also
operates one of the most extensive pro-Israel advocacy networks in the world.
The organization's first executive director was [Irwin
Katsof](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/display_990/61611859/2002_12_EO%2F06-1611859_990_200112?__cf_chl_f_tk=nKvFoS_BdvkoB.PowTtzHONuS_dCedmOJOQqZycrLA4-1782825953-1.0.1.1-m3Ppg2F4rObiDDsYuE1gADbeorhjL4FOYooU5FnfGGE),
who simultaneously served as president of the Jerusalem Fund. In 2001, the
Jerusalem Fund lent the newly established Middle East Media Watch (Honest
Reporting's registered name at the time) $158,724. The following year, Aish
HaTorah's Jerusalem operation provided a further $48,100 grant.

Honest Reporting's 2006 tax return lists [Ephraim
Shore](https://aish.com/authors/48866822/), who heads Aish's operations in
Israel, as president. Shore is also one of the founders of the Hasbara
Fellowships program--the Israeli Foreign Ministry's campus advocacy initiative
that Aish HaTorah was asked to develop and run. His twin brother, Raphael
Shore, produced "Obsession: Radical Islam's War Against the West," a
controversial 2005 film that Honest Reporting initially promoted as its own
project on its website and listed as an affiliate in 2006, before later
[denying any
involvement](https://typeinvestigations.org/investigation/2008/10/29/aish-
hatorahs-new-obsession/) in its production.

When the Israeli Foreign Ministry sought to counter what it characterized as
anti-Israel sentiment on university campuses internationally, it turned to
Aish HaTorah to design and run the program, which flies hundreds of student
leaders to Israel for intensive advocacy training. Multiple current Honest
Reporting staff members worked as Hasbara Fellowship lecturers.

The financial relationship between Aish HaTorah and Honest Reporting has not
been confined to the founding period. Canadian tax filings
[show](https://www.charitydata.ca/charity/hr-canada-charitable-
organization/799547534RR0001/) that Honest Reporting Canada made a donation of
$15,000 to Aish HaTorah as recently as 2023, demonstrating that the
institutional relationship between the two organizations remains active more
than two decades after Honest Reporting's founding.

The network around Honest Reporting extends to some of the most controversial
pro-Israel blacklisting operations on the internet, including Canary Mission,
the pro-Israel doxxing site that publishes dossiers on students, academics,
and activists it accused of anti-Semitism or support for Palestinian rights.
At least one former employee of [Honest
Reporting](https://honestreporting.com/author/zahava900hr/page/2/?__cf_chl_f_tk=D_lBmnExfHcJbW8P2dBz2fTX1lbyVPOLe9pM4HbF.cY-1782839823-1.0.1.1-OwjJSU3uGh4BKyH2F7vB3iqRc4XznUw90lhy8EaE_.Y),[
Zahava Raymond](https://forward.com/news/411355/revealed-canary-mission-
blacklist-is-secretly-bankrolled-by-major-jewish/) has worked at [Megamot
Shalom](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/canary-mission-israel-megamot-shalom-
highest-paid-employees), the Israeli nonprofit organization funding Canary
Mission.

## **A Widening Operation**

According to Honest Reporting's filings with Israel's Corporations Authority,
96.6% of the total 2024 budget of 6,040,198 NIS [$1,632,044] comes from
foreign donations. In addition to the $100,000 grant from the Knight
Foundation, 4,903,640 NIS [$1,324,950] came directly from Honest Reporting's
U.S. organization. The Israeli operation is almost entirely dependent on
American dollars.

Honest Reporting's recent
[communications](https://www.facebook.com/DalitMarxists/posts/pfbid02D2YN4rZPEbREpcBJavo71QN9hj6Z8wZeuZUeCQ6jhnamcYzSvANBga1Ju8WH7ne3l)
demonstrate the group's growing ambitions. An update to supporters describes
the launch of "Honest Reporting AI Labs," a proprietary system trained to
identify "anti-Israel bias" and intercept narratives "before they reach
mainstream credibility." The system monitors social media in real time, traces
what the organization characterizes as "coordinated narrative pipelines," and
feeds findings to what it calls "strategic communications partners," among
them the Foundation for Defense of Democracies.

In May, for example, Rachel O'Donoghue, an employee of Honest Reporting, was
[invited](https://honestreporting.com/exposing-media-falsehoods-and-shaping-
the-narrative-honestreporting-is-making-an-impact/) to publish a column in the
[Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/opinion/free-expression/kristofs-
unbelievable-tale-d9d7b6ff) challenging Nicolas Kristoff's article in the New
York Times about Israel's use of sexual violence against Palestinian
detainees. The organization's research has also been cited in articles
published by the [Washington Free
Beacon](https://freebeacon.com/israel/committee-to-protect-journalists-staff-
is-revealed-to-be-packed-with-anti-israel-agitators-amid-boardroom-feuds-over-
groups-list-of-journalists-killed-in-gaza/) and [National
Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/news/kristofs-extraordinary-claims-
about-israeli-rape-require-extraordinary-evidence-the-times-doesnt-have-it/).

The reach of Honest Reporting and its affiliates extends into the legislative
institutions of its English-speaking donor base. In 2018, Honest Reporting
submitted
[evidence](https://data.parliament.uk/writtenevidence/committeeevidence.svc/evidencedocument/digital-
culture-media-and-sport-committee/fake-news/written/79211.pdf) to the UK
Parliament's inquiry into fake news, falsely claiming that "Honest Reporting
is not aligned with any government or political party or movement." The
submission was initially [absent](https://www.uklfi.com/uklfi-pushes-israel-
into-parliaments-fake-news-enquiry) from the inquiry's published record and
was only made available following the intervention of UK Lawyers for Israel.

The Canadian operation has demonstrated similar objectives. In July 2023,
Honest Reporting Canada's executive director Mike Fegelman
[said](https://www.jns.org/antisemitism/honestreporting-canada-we-want-to-
create-a-digital-army-for-israel) it wanted to "create a digital army for
Israel." A [written
briefing](https://www.ourcommons.ca/Content/Committee/451/CHPC/Brief/BR13948792/br-
external/HonestReportingCanada-e.pdf) to the House of Commons' Standing
Committee on Canadian Heritage referred to Palestinian journalists killed by
Israel as "so-called journalists" with "connections to Palestinian terrorist
groups" and claimed media coverage of Gaza "directly contributes to a spike in
anti-Jewish hate crimes."

Another significant donor identified in Honest Reporting's 2024 Israeli
filings is a vaguely named organization called Canadian Charity Partners,
which contributed 507,176 NIS [$137,000]. In January 2026, the Canada Revenue
Agency [revoked](https://www.canadiancharitylaw.ca/blog/cra-revokes-
charitable-status-of-canada-charity-partners/) Canadian Charity Partners'
charitable status, citing multiple areas of non-compliance including
conducting non-charitable activities and failing to maintain adequate books
and records.

Honest Reporting Canada has run its own pressure campaigns against journalists
and outlets it deems biased against Israel, claiming to have contributed to
the dismissal of two Palestinian journalists in October 2023, one of whom was
on maternity leave at the time. In November 2024, [Robert
Walker](https://honestreporting.ca/team-members/robert-walker/), the group's
assistant director, [was arrested and faced 17 criminal
charges](https://www.timesofisrael.com/employee-at-canadian-pro-israel-media-
watchdog-charged-for-anti-palestinian-graffiti/) in connection with a string
of anti-Palestinian graffiti in Toronto, including the phrase "Fuck Gaza." The
charges were [withdrawn](https://www.thestar.com/news/crime/crown-withdraws-
charges-against-honest-reporting-staffer-over-anti-palestinian-
graffiti/article_31e9f58c-f909-11ef-8b13-f712e169b30e.html) in March 2025
after a payment to charity. Walker remains employed by the organization.
